topic: Connected Environment: control paths and the building blocks for a future AI agent
summary: Connected Environment's backend already contains the building blocks for a future AI agent, all Weather Station scoped: a secured MCP endpoint inside the backend with 33 permission-gated tools (26 read, 4 propose, 3 observer bookkeeping), a deterministic safety verdict with an advisory work decision and an optional, fallback-protected AI wording layer, five agent-monitoring evidence reads, an observer control plane where agents draft and only people decide, zero-write observation previews with approval-gated send, and a propose-then-second-person-approves change spine. The human-approval invariant is enforced by a separate approval scope, a self-approval refusal, diff echo, and IL-walking tests that prove no MCP code reaches approval, direct writes or the review operations. On 2026-10-04 the production gateway serves the MCP discovery document and a 401 challenge, and the observer, agent-observation, approval, audit, safety-policy and gas-acknowledge routes all exist in production, but no running agent, no connected client and no approver token is evidenced, the Observation Manager link is built for Weather and Lightning only (Gas is NOT built, a Todo created today), Lightning email/SMS was removed, and the portal's agent composition and observation drawer are shipped but flag-gated default OFF with unknown production state. Of the 'one language' claims: one backend is confirmed, one permission family is confirmed for reads (writes differ), one rule set is refuted, and one audit trail is refuted (audit covers weather policy only). Control is real but not a two-person chokepoint: a manage-weather-settings holder publishes policy directly with version check, loosening acknowledgement and audit.

mcp_tools.name: get_indicators
mcp_tools.what_it_does_plain: Current live sensor readings for a project (temperature, humidity, heat index, wind, gases and the rest), as the dashboard shows them; optionally one station. Needs read access to Weather Station (view) or project manage.

mcp_tools.name: get_graphs
mcp_tools.what_it_does_plain: Which time-series graphs a project has, with names, units and current summaries. Needs read access to Weather Station (view) or project manage.

mcp_tools.name: get_graph_hour
mcp_tools.what_it_does_plain: One hour of one graph (temperature or wind speed only) for today. Needs read access to Weather Station (view) or project manage.
evidence: Server time zone applies, no explicit conversion: wakecap-weather-station/Wakecap.WeatherStation.Web.API/Mcp/Tools/DashboardTools.cs:70-73

mcp_tools.name: get_historical
mcp_tools.what_it_does_plain: Averaged readings over a time range, for trends. Needs read access to Weather Station (view) or project manage.

mcp_tools.name: get_thresholds
mcp_tools.what_it_does_plain: The project's configured alert limits, read uncached so an agent never acts on a limit a safety officer already changed. Needs read access to Weather Station (view) or project manage.
evidence: wakecap-weather-station/Wakecap.WeatherStation.Web.API/Mcp/Tools/ConfigurationTools.cs:41-45 (skipCache: true). Side effect: on a project with none, the read creates default thresholds (wakecap-weather-station/Wakecap.WeatherStation.Web.API/Mcp/Tools/ConfigurationTools.cs:32-33).

mcp_tools.name: get_project_settings
mcp_tools.what_it_does_plain: Unit system, heat-index calculation method and per-sensor online flags. Needs read access to Weather Station (view) or project manage.

mcp_tools.name: get_heat_index_bands
mcp_tools.what_it_does_plain: The project's resolved heat-index risk bands (label, colour, range, project override or platform default). Needs read access to Weather Station (view) or project manage.

mcp_tools.name: get_station_health
mcp_tools.what_it_does_plain: Backend-computed health of the station(s): live, stale, dark, suspect or unknown, with anomaly kinds (stuck, missing, sentinel, impossible). Adds no classification of its own. Needs read access to Weather Station (view) or project manage.

mcp_tools.name: get_agent_summary
mcp_tools.what_it_does_plain: The full deterministic safety summary: verdict, reasons, recommended actions, station health, priority cards, work decision, dashboard recommendations. Needs read access to Weather Station (view) or project manage.

mcp_tools.name: get_weather_stations_status
mcp_tools.what_it_does_plain: Registration and connectivity of every weather station in a project (online, stale, suspect, dark, offline, unregistered). Vocabulary differs from get_station_health on purpose. Needs read access to Weather Station (view) or project manage.

mcp_tools.name: get_weather_stations_summary
mcp_tools.what_it_does_plain: Project roll-up of station readiness with per-state counts and reasons. Needs read access to Weather Station (view) or project manage.

mcp_tools.name: get_weather_station_insight
mcp_tools.what_it_does_plain: One station's insight view: header state plus the reading collections behind it. Needs read access to Weather Station (view) or project manage.

mcp_tools.name: get_project_monitoring_snapshot
mcp_tools.what_it_does_plain: One bounded poll that composes readings, station health, safety verdict, thresholds and settings with per-source success or failure, so one failed source is never mistaken for a dark project. MCP only: no REST route serves it. Needs read access to Weather Station (view) or project manage.

mcp_tools.name: get_dashboard_layout
mcp_tools.what_it_does_plain: A user's saved dashboard layout (featured cards, order, dismissed recommendations). Per user per project, not a project setting. Needs read access to Weather Station (view) or project manage.

mcp_tools.name: validate_dashboard_layout
mcp_tools.what_it_does_plain: Checks a proposed layout against the card catalogue and reports every rule broken; saves nothing. Needs read access to Weather Station (view) or project manage.

mcp_tools.name: get_station_reading_window
mcp_tools.what_it_does_plain: Individual sensor readings for one station in a UTC window (max 7 days, newest N per sensor, default 500), each with its quality; suspect readings carry no value. Needs read access to Weather Station (view) or project manage.

mcp_tools.name: get_station_capabilities
mcp_tools.what_it_does_plain: What one station is expected to measure (sensors, units). Sample cadence is null: not modelled anywhere. Needs read access to Weather Station (view) or project manage.

mcp_tools.name: get_project_operating_context
mcp_tools.what_it_does_plain: Unit system and heat-index method needed to interpret readings; time zone, operating hours and policy version are omitted because no data exists for them. Needs read access to Weather Station (view) or project manage.

mcp_tools.name: get_station_maintenance_state
mcp_tools.what_it_does_plain: Whether a station is in a planned maintenance window. Always reports not_tracked today (no table exists), which means unknown, not 'no maintenance'. Needs read access to Weather Station (view) or project manage.

mcp_tools.name: get_weather_service_health
mcp_tools.what_it_does_plain: Readiness of the weather API and its dependencies, to tell an infrastructure fault from every station genuinely going dark. Needs read access to Weather Station (view) or project manage.

mcp_tools.name: get_change_audit_history
mcp_tools.what_it_does_plain: The append-only safety-configuration change trail, newest first, including conflicted, rejected and failed attempts, keyset-paged. Note: the MCP tool needs only the read pair while the REST audit route needs the manage-weather-settings permission (deliberate, McpToolPermissions.cs:20-25). Needs read access to Weather Station (view) or project manage.

mcp_tools.name: get_change_request
mcp_tools.what_it_does_plain: One change request and its status (pending, approved, applied, rejected, expired, stale, failed), scoped to the project. Needs read access to Weather Station (view) or project manage.

mcp_tools.name: list_pending_change_requests
mcp_tools.what_it_does_plain: Change requests still waiting for a human to approve. Needs read access to Weather Station (view) or project manage.

mcp_tools.name: preview_agent_observation
mcp_tools.what_it_does_plain: Lists every observation the platform could report about one station right now, built from the same evaluation as the dashboard; writes, proposes and sends nothing. Marks each as 'sent automatically' or 'needs approval'. Needs read access to Weather Station (view) or project manage.

mcp_tools.name: get_observer_checkpoint
mcp_tools.what_it_does_plain: The observer's durable cursor (where its last completed cycle got to) for one named observer. Needs read access to Weather Station (view) or project manage.

mcp_tools.name: list_open_findings
mcp_tools.what_it_does_plain: Findings the agent has drafted that a human has not resolved (open, acknowledged, snoozed). Needs read access to Weather Station (view) or project manage.

mcp_tools.name: propose_set_threshold
mcp_tools.what_it_does_plain: Creates a PENDING proposal to change the alert limits (complete state, range-checked). Applies nothing; a human with approval permission must approve out of band. Needs edit or project manage; this is permission to propose or keep notes, never to approve.
evidence: wakecap-weather-station/Wakecap.WeatherStation.IntegrationTests/McpToolSurfaceTests.cs:232-237 (proposal tools state plainly nothing is applied)

mcp_tools.name: propose_update_settings
mcp_tools.what_it_does_plain: Creates a PENDING proposal to change project settings (unit, heat-index method). Cannot change a sensor's online flag. Applies nothing. Needs edit or project manage; this is permission to propose or keep notes, never to approve.

mcp_tools.name: propose_set_indicator_enabled
mcp_tools.what_it_does_plain: Creates a PENDING proposal to set one sensor online or offline (absolute state, not a toggle). Applies nothing. Needs edit or project manage; this is permission to propose or keep notes, never to approve.

mcp_tools.name: propose_agent_observation
mcp_tools.what_it_does_plain: Creates a PENDING proposal to report an observation to the Observation Manager; only 'station not reporting' and 'frozen sensor' can be proposed; the backend rebuilds all wording and numbers, the agent supplies identifiers only. Sends nothing until a second person approves; proposal lapses after 24 hours. Needs edit or project manage; this is permission to propose or keep notes, never to approve.

mcp_tools.name: set_observer_checkpoint
mcp_tools.what_it_does_plain: Advances the observer's own cursor by compare-and-swap. The agent's own bookkeeping, not a proposal: changes no weather data, threshold or setting. Needs edit or project manage; this is permission to propose or keep notes, never to approve.

mcp_tools.name: create_finding_draft
mcp_tools.what_it_does_plain: Drafts a finding for a human to review, or appends evidence if that condition already has one (deduplicated by a database index). The agent drafts; it cannot acknowledge, snooze or resolve. Needs edit or project manage; this is permission to propose or keep notes, never to approve.

mcp_tools.name: update_finding_evidence
mcp_tools.what_it_does_plain: Appends a newer evidence sample to an unresolved finding without changing its status. Needs edit or project manage; this is permission to propose or keep notes, never to approve.

agent_blocks.name: MCP endpoint inside the backend
agent_blocks.what_plain: A secured interface (path /mcp) on the same service as the portal's own API, so an AI agent can call the same functions under the same sign-in and permissions. Not a separate service.
evidence: [live 2026-10-04] unauthenticated POST https://services.wakecap.com/weather-station/mcp -> HTTP 401 with WWW-Authenticate: Bearer resource_metadata="https://services.wakecap.com/weather-station/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp"; GET -> 405 allow: POST

agent_blocks.name: 33-tool MCP surface (26 read, 7 write)
agent_blocks.what_plain: 26 tools that only read, 4 that only raise pending proposals, 3 that keep the agent's own notes. None approves anything and none writes safety settings directly. Weather Station data only: there are no Lightning or Gas tools.
evidence: wakecap-weather-station/README.md:424-426 ('33 tools: 26 read, 4 propose, 3 observer writes')

Tool list itself needs a bearer token so was not enumerated live. The observer controller from the same commit as the 5 observer tools answers 401 in production (route exists), so the 33-tool build is very likely deployed; not proven.

agent_blocks.name: OAuth discovery for MCP clients (RFC 9728)
agent_blocks.what_plain: A public document that tells an agent client where to sign in. It advertises the authorization server and the scopes.
evidence: [live 2026-10-04] production document advertises authorization_servers ["http://identity-service.prod.svc.cluster.local:4009"], a cluster-internal address an outside client cannot reach. INTERNAL DEFECT CANDIDATE, see open_questions.

agent_blocks.name: Agent summary (deterministic verdict + work decision)
agent_blocks.what_plain: One read that returns the site's safety verdict, reasons, recommended actions, station health and a work decision (safe to work, controlled work, stop work, safety unknown), all from fixed rules.
evidence: [live 2026-10-04] GET .../api/project/{id}/AgentSummary unauthenticated -> 401 (route exists; a non-existent route returned 404)

agent_blocks.name: Optional AI wording layer (narrator) with deterministic fallback
agent_blocks.what_plain: An optional pass that lets Claude reword the human-facing text only. If it is off, has no key, times out or fails, the plain deterministic text is returned unchanged. It cannot change status, numbers, thresholds or actions.
evidence: wakecap-weather-station/Wakecap.WeatherStation.Core/Products/WeatherStation/Services/Agent/AgentNarrator.cs:39-54 (disabled / no key -> unchanged), :102-107 (any failure -> unchanged), :116-127 (authoritative fields carried over)
release-deck/ws-release-2026-08.html:337 ('Claude narration dark in prod' as of the August deck; no later evidence found)

agent_blocks.name: Five permission-gated agent-monitoring reads
agent_blocks.what_plain: Five read-only evidence reads an agent reasons over: a station's reading window, its capabilities, the project operating context, maintenance state and weather-service health.
evidence: Three of the five return stubs by design: capability cadence null, operating-context time zone/hours/policy version null, maintenance state always not_tracked (AgentMonitoringController.cs:85-95, :108-112, :136-138).

agent_blocks.name: Project monitoring snapshot
agent_blocks.what_plain: One bounded read that gathers readings, health, verdict, limits and settings, each tagged ok or failed.
evidence: Reachable only through MCP; no REST controller uses IProjectMonitoringSnapshotService (grep of Web.API).

agent_blocks.name: Change proposal endpoint
agent_blocks.what_plain: Lets an agent or a person with edit rights raise a pending change request that applies nothing. Must carry the complete target state. Expires after 24 hours.

agent_blocks.name: Change approval endpoint (human-only)
agent_blocks.what_plain: The only door that applies an approved change. Needs a separate approval permission on the person's token, a second person (not the proposer), the exact stored change echoed back, and a written reason.
evidence: [live 2026-10-04] route exists (405 allow: POST on GET)
Whether any production token actually carries the approval scope is unknown.

agent_blocks.name: Observer control plane (agent drafts, human decides)
agent_blocks.what_plain: A separate area with its own tables where an agent can keep a cursor, draft findings and add evidence, and where only a person can acknowledge, snooze or resolve a finding.
evidence: Merged 2026-10-01 (commit 41b20bf). Known gap in commit message: its Postgres suite ObserverFindingWritePathTests is not yet in the CI database job.

agent_blocks.name: Agent observations (zero-write preview, approval-gated send)
agent_blocks.what_plain: An engineer or agent can preview what could be reported about a station. Two kinds (station not reporting, frozen sensor) can be sent to the Observation Manager, but only after a second person approves.
evidence: [live 2026-10-04] POST route .../AgentObservations/preview exists (405 allow: POST on GET)
Whether the Observation Manager notifies anyone for these types depends on routing outside this repo.

agent_blocks.name: Observation outbox and dispatcher (Weather Station)
agent_blocks.what_plain: Safety breaches are written once per episode into a queue and delivered to the Observation Manager with retries; a second delivery of the same episode is refused.
evidence: Runs whenever the app runs; sink URL and Observation Manager acceptance in production were not verified. History: dispatch was switched off by hotfix 5869f6d (404 storm) then made unconditional by 0349c35.

agent_blocks.name: Observation outbox and dispatcher (Lightning)
agent_blocks.what_plain: When a lightning device enters Red, Fault or Offline, an observation row is saved with the state change and delivered to the Observation Manager with retries.
evidence: wakecap-weather-station/Wakecap.WeatherStation.Core/Products/LightningSensor/Hosting/LightningQueueConsumerBackgroundService.cs:44-55 (consumer idles when no queue URL is configured)
[live 2026-10-04] route .../lightning-sensor/Devices/observations exists (401). Whether the production queues are configured and a device is feeding is unknown.

agent_blocks.name: Dashboard composition recommendations (layout mode, promoted cards, dynamic charts)
agent_blocks.what_plain: The safety service recommends what the dashboard should foreground and which up-to-three charts explain the decision. A recommendation only: the saved layout wins and the engineer accepts or dismisses.
evidence: frontend-2.0-weather-station/src/app/features/WeatherStation/agent-dashboard/hooks/useAgentDashboardComposition.ts:12-13, :33 (only an explicit true turns it on)
[live-bundle 2026-10-04] production bundle 1.0.5 contains the code and the flag name; the flag's value in production is not readable without the flag service.

agent_blocks.name: Observation drawer in the portal (request approval / approve)
agent_blocks.what_plain: Inside the dashboard, a person can see what could be reported, ask a second person to approve it, and an approver can approve it with a written reason. Shown only when the composition flag is on.
evidence: [live-bundle] production bundle 1.0.5 contains the drawer strings ('Nothing is sent until they approve, and the request lapses after 24 hours').

agent_blocks.name: A running AI agent that polls sites and proposes actions
agent_blocks.what_plain: An agent that actually runs against sites. No such runner exists in any repo; the building blocks above are what it would use.
evidence: No agent loop or scheduler in the backend: grep for hosted/background services named agent or observer in Core returned nothing; 'dark-station-watch' appears only as a doc example in ObserverTools.cs:41 and ObserverCheckpoint.cs:26.

control_paths.what: Publish the site safety policy (limits, per-sensor Counted switch, heat-index bands) in one act
control_paths.how_plain: A person with the weather-policy management permission edits and publishes the whole policy together, all or nothing. It is refused if someone else changed it first (version check), refused if it loosens any limit unless the person explicitly acknowledges the loosening, and every change is written to the audit trail. When a policy is published, open alert episodes are closed against the new policy so alerts restart under the new rules.
evidence: [live 2026-10-04] PUT .../SafetyPolicy route exists (405 allow: PUT on GET)
Direct publish is NOT second-person approval. See must_not_claim.

control_paths.what: Direct threshold, settings, heat-index-band and sensor-online writes
control_paths.how_plain: The same management permission can still write each resource directly, version-checked where a version is supplied and audited. These direct writes do not go through the second-person approval route.

control_paths.what: Propose a change, a second person approves (out-of-band approval)
control_paths.how_plain: Anyone with edit rights, or an agent, raises a pending change request with the complete new state. Another person holding the separate approval permission approves it by echoing the exact stored change and giving a reason. If the target moved meanwhile, the approval is refused and the request goes stale. Requests expire after 24 hours.
evidence: wakecap-weather-station/Wakecap.WeatherStation.IntegrationTests/ChangeApprovalServiceTests.cs:74,96,119,156 (diff mismatch, self-approval, cross-project, second approval refused)
Whether any production user token carries the approval scope is unknown (identity-owner gate G16 in the Zero-Open plan, line 169).

control_paths.how_plain: The Settings screen can read the append-only change trail (who, when, what changed, including refused and failed attempts), a single change request, the pending list, a table stating which kinds of change are audited and which are not, and an export with a checksum.
evidence: frontend-2.0-weather-station/src/app/features/WeatherStation/policy/changeHistoryFlag.ts:31 (history tab on unless flag explicitly false)
Export is behind a feature switch: ChangeAuditController.cs:200 (ChangeAuditExportFeature.IsEnabled); state in production unknown.

control_paths.what: Safety observations delivered to the Observation Manager automatically (Weather Station)
control_paths.how_plain: When a reading breaches a limit or enters a heat-index band, the episode is recorded once and sent to the Observation Manager with retries, without anyone approving it. Clearing is recorded too.

When a lightning device newly enters Red, Fault or Offline, an observation is saved with the state change and sent to the Observation Manager. Orange and Yellow do not raise one. 'Sent' means the Observation Manager accepted it, not that a person was alerted.
evidence: wakecap-weather-station/Wakecap.WeatherStation.Core/Products/LightningSensor/Services/LightningIngestService.cs:88-102 (only on a changed state from a live packet)

wakecap-weather-station/Wakecap.WeatherStation.Web.API/Products/LightningSensor/Controllers/DevicesController.cs:113-121 (send status: Sent, Pending, Retrying, Failed; 'Sent means accepted, not that a person has been alerted')
No portal screen lists lightning observations: no 'observations' reference under frontend LightningSensor feature.

control_paths.how_plain: The platform's own lightning email, SMS and portal notification engine, alert-routing and alerts endpoints were deleted; alerting is owned by the Observation Manager. State, staleness and history are unchanged.
evidence: wakecap-weather-station commit 367bf43 (2026-09-24) 'TAN-1901: remove lightning notifications (Observation Manager owns alerting)'
grep of Core/Products/LightningSensor and Web.API/Products/LightningSensor for sms|email|notification finds no live notification code
[live-bundle] production FE bundle 1.0.5 does not contain 'Alerts sent to the alarming service' (0 hits); FE commit 51b74dd removed that panel

control_paths.what: Lightning alarm distances and all-clear delay
control_paths.how_plain: A person with the lightning-management permission sets the red and yellow alarm radii (km) and the all-clear delay (minutes) per device in Settings. Not version-checked or audited.
evidence: wakecap-weather-station/Wakecap.WeatherStation.Domain/Shared/Entity/ChangeAuditCoverage.cs:243-252 (lightning writes 'off the TAN-2020 version and audit spine entirely')

control_paths.how_plain: A person with edit or manage rights can acknowledge an alert (seen it) or close it. Who and when are recorded on the alert from the sign-in, never typed. Two people acting at once cannot overwrite each other. Nothing is sent back to the vendor's own system: an alert closed here stays open there. If the gas is still over its limit, the next reading raises a new alert.
evidence: wakecap-weather-station/Wakecap.WeatherStation.Domain/Shared/Entity/ChangeAuditCoverage.cs:265-281 (not in the change audit; the alert row itself carries who/when)
[live 2026-10-04] POST .../gas-detector/Alerts/{id}/acknowledge route exists (405 allow: POST on GET)
[live-bundle] 'Acknowledge' and 'Close alert' strings present in production bundle 1.0.5 (FE commit 7f5eef0)

control_paths.how_plain: Read-only today: the portal can show which limits each gas is judged against, but there is no write route for gas limits.
evidence: Every gas controller method is a GET except zone assignment (DevicesController.cs:106-107), acknowledge and close (AlertsController.cs:50,70) and the vendor push receiver (GasPushController.cs:41,58).

control_paths.what: Gas alert to Observation Manager hand-off
control_paths.how_plain: NOT BUILT. A gas alarm exists only on the Gas screens and in the platform's own alert table; nothing is sent to the Observation Manager or to anyone it notifies.
evidence: grep -i observation over Core/Products/GasDetector, Web.API/Products/GasDetector, Domain/Products/GasDetector, Contracts/Products/GasDetector returns nothing
wakecap-weather-station/Wakecap.WeatherStation.Domain/Products/WeatherStation/Entity/WeatherObservation.cs:96-101 (ObservationSource.Gas constant exists; grep shows nothing ever writes it)
Linear TAN-2943 (created 2026-10-04, status Todo): 'checked on master, 2026-10-04: no Gas code references it'; earlier plan TAN-2447 archived 2026-10-01
[live-bundle] the only 'Observation Manager' strings in production bundle 1.0.5 belong to the weather observation drawer

control_paths.what: Observer finding review (acknowledge, snooze, resolve) by a person
control_paths.how_plain: Only a person with the separate review permission can mark a drafted finding as seen, hold it for up to seven days with a reason, or close it with a written resolution; each action records who, when and why in the finding's own history.
evidence: No portal screen for observer findings: 0 hits for ObserverFindings in production bundle 1.0.5 and no FE feature references it. REST only.

claims.claim: MCP is a second transport inside the existing backend host, not a separate service; stateless streamable HTTP at /mcp, authenticated by the same JWT bearer as the REST API.

evidence.quote: The server runs inside this ASP.NET Core application rather than beside it.

claims.safe_phrase: The platform has a secured interface built for AI agents. It sits on the same service and uses the same sign-in as the portal.
claims.caveats: Live: production /mcp answers 401 with a discovery hint (2026-10-04). Do not say any agent is using it.

claims.claim: 33 MCP tools: 26 read-only, 4 propose-only, 3 observer bookkeeping writes. All Weather Station scoped; no Lightning or Gas tool exists.
claims.safe_phrase: An agent can read the site's weather readings, limits, safety verdict and change history, and can only suggest changes.
claims.caveats: Do not state a tool count in a video. The August deck's '16 tools (13 read + 3 write)' is superseded by 33. Weather only: do not imply an agent can read Lightning or Gas through this interface today.

claims.claim: Every tool is permission-gated on the same permission constants as the matching REST endpoint, fail-closed (a tool with no entry is unreachable), and tools/list shows a caller only the tools they may call.

evidence.quote: Fail closed. McpToolAuthorizationFilter refuses any tool name absent from this map.

claims.safe_phrase: An agent sees and can use only what the person it acts for is allowed to see and do.
claims.caveats: Authorization is evaluated per tenant and permission through the admin permission service; the project id is a tool argument and is not passed to that check (McpToolAuthorizer.cs:321-328). Do not claim project-level isolation for MCP without confirming it matches REST.

claims.claim: The human-approval invariant: an agent may propose, never approve. No MCP tool reaches the approval route, a direct write, the store or the observation outbox; proven against compiled IL, plus REST scope gates.

evidence.quote: the only write path this transport has, and it does not write.
this transport exposes no tool that reaches that route and no tool that reaches the direct threshold, settings or indicator PUTs.

claims.safe_phrase: The agent can suggest. Only a person can approve, and the platform enforces that, not just the policy.
claims.caveats: Enforced in code and tests [code]. Live: the approval route exists in production. Not verified: that production approver tokens exist or that the approval scope is issued. A person who holds the separate management permission can still write policy directly (see C13).

claims.claim: Approval needs: the weather.change.approve scope on the token, a second party (proposer subject must differ), the stored diff echoed byte-for-byte, and a reviewer note; approval is recorded before the change is applied; a target that moved makes the request stale instead of overwriting.
claims.safe_phrase: A suggested change is shown to a second person exactly as proposed. They approve it with a written reason, and the change is refused if the setting has moved since.
claims.caveats: Proposals lapse after 24 hours (ChangeProposalService.cs:67).

claims.claim: The agent summary's every safety-bearing field comes from deterministic rules; an optional Claude pass may reword human-facing text only and falls back to the deterministic text on any failure, no key, or switch off.

evidence.quote: Every safety-bearing field — status, severity, confidence, numbers, thresholds and the recommended actions themselves — is produced by deterministic rules.

claims.safe_phrase: The safety verdict comes from fixed rules, never from an AI model. Any AI wording is optional, and the plain text is used if it is unavailable.
claims.caveats: Whether wording enrichment is switched on in production is unknown; the August deck says it was dark then (release-deck:337). Do not claim the portal shows AI-written text.

claims.claim: workDecision (safe_to_work, controlled_work, stop_work, safety_unknown) is a total fixed projection of the verdict status (danger->stop_work, caution->controlled_work, safe->safe_to_work, anything else->safety_unknown); advisory, so it can never disagree with the verdict.

evidence.quote: public static string MapDecision(string? verdictStatus) => verdictStatus switch

claims.safe_phrase: The platform turns each safety verdict into plain guidance: safe to work, work with controls, stop work, or safety unknown.
claims.caveats: workDecision is NOT read by the current portal front end (no 'workDecision' in frontend src); it exists for agents and API consumers. Do not say the portal displays a 'work decision' field.

claims.claim: criteriaVersion identifies the heat-index criteria applied (band name, bounds, work/rest/water cadence, no-work flag; 'hi=none' if none), NOT the whole policy: editing a gas or dust limit leaves it unchanged.

evidence.quote: It does NOT cover the configured indicator thresholds (CO, H2S, PM10, ...).

claims.safe_phrase: Every decision records which heat rules it was made under.
claims.caveats: Never describe it as a version of the whole safety policy.

claims.claim: The five agent-monitoring reads exist and are permission-gated; three return honest stubs: capability cadence null, operating context omits time zone/hours/policy version, maintenance state always 'not_tracked'.

evidence.quote: NEEDS DATA MODEL: No maintenance-state table exists. Always returns trackingState="not_tracked"

claims.safe_phrase: The platform exposes the evidence an agent needs: recent readings, what each station should measure, site context and service health.
claims.caveats: Do not claim planned-maintenance awareness; it is not tracked.

open_questions: Production MCP discovery advertises authorization_servers = a cluster-internal URL (http://identity-service.prod.svc.cluster.local:4009). An external MCP client cannot reach that. Is IdentityService:Authority meant to be internal for token validation with a separate public issuer for discovery? Also the Zero-Open plan names an IdentityServer 'WakecapMCP' allowed-scope gate (G16, line 169), while the metadata advertises scope 'MainApp'. Needs the identity owner.

Does any production token (human or service) carry weather.change.approve or weather.observer.review? Without them the approval flow and the finding review exist but cannot be used. Not readable from the repos.

Is weather-station-agent-dashboard-composition ON for any production user? Flag service not readable here. Needs a screen capture from a signed-in production session before any video shows composition or the observation drawer.
Is the Claude narration key/enable switch set in production? August deck says dark; no newer evidence. Check live: AgentSummary incidentSummary on a danger verdict.

Is the Observation Manager sink URL healthy in production and does the Observation Manager route weather and lightning types to anyone? Dispatch was disabled by hotfix in September then re-enabled; no delivery evidence found.
Are the lightning queue URLs configured in production and is any device feeding? The consumer idles when no queue URL is set (LightningQueueConsumerBackgroundService.cs:44-55).

Does the MCP permission check scope to the project? McpToolAuthorizer asks the admin service by tenant and permission only (McpToolAuthorizer.cs:321-328) and projectId is a tool argument; confirm REST does the same and that an agent token cannot read a project it has no rights on.
ChangeAuditController.Export is behind a feature switch (ChangeAuditExportFeature); production value unknown.
The observer's Postgres suite (ObserverFindingWritePathTests) was not in the CI database job when merged on 2026-10-01 (commit message); confirm it was added.

FE bundle 1.0.5 is production per the task; the repo has no tag for it and the audit ledger's '1.0.5' was a testing build on 2026-08-27. The mapping used here (bundle strings match FE master through 95e1650) is inferred from served-bundle content, not from a release record.
